recommendations.rationale: The final saved projected state (update 34) has an effective horizon of 1 control interval, matching the authorized 0.01 s horizon, so a local_comparison with exactly one adopted weight change is scope-permissible; however it measures only local plan/endpoint differences and cannot establish closed-loop settling or attribute the residual tip speed, so it is deferred pending adoption in a later phase.

A prediction_braking comparison at the final saved projected state over the fixed 0.01 s horizon can measure local endpoint speed/position differences between recorded input and an instantaneous braking-box input, but cannot separate objective weighting, seed selection, effective-horizon truncation, or backend-model mismatch when they predict the same local endpoint; deferred pending adoption.

Complete coverage reads of the earlier sampled backend motion and one-step predictions (updates 0–26) are recommended before any check, to confirm whether the residual tip speed develops only within the final window; deferred to a later phase.

attribution.reason: Recorded recipe weights (tracking 1.0; velocity 1e-4; terminal_velocity 1e-4; tension 1e-4) are raw magnitudes with no retained cost-term contributions, so whether the terminal-velocity term governs the residual speed is not observable; the recorded one-step endpoint differences (tip differences ~1e-3–5e-3 m, velocity vector differences ~0.10–0.12 m/s) are compatible with several hypotheses.

Selections are recorded (initialization_selected=29, noninitialization_selected=6) with policy stop reasons such as relative_seed_improvement and budget_best_feasible, but the full warm plans and optimizer iteration traces required to separate seed/initialization choice from objective weighting are not retained.

The per-update effective horizon shrinks to a single 0.01 s control interval by update 34 versus the configured 10; a one-interval problem limits braking lookahead and is consistent with residual tip speed, but the retained local checks cannot establish it as the dominant settling cause.

The retained one-step comparisons (projected GVS prediction versus full serial-backend endpoint) show only small tip/velocity differences and are explicitly scoped as recorded projected states, not full backend-state error, so they do not separate model mismatch from weighting, seed, or horizon effects.

facts.statement: The retained execution reports reach_passed=true with terminal_error_m≈0.00764 m inside the 0.01 m reach tolerance, while sampled_settling_passed=false with late_max_error_m≈0.0581 m and late_max_speed_m_s≈1.581 m/s against the settling limits 0.01 m and 0.02 m/s over a 0.05 s window.

Per-update effective horizon decreases across the final window: 8 (update 27), 6 (29), 5 (30), 4 (31), 3 (32), 2 (33), 1 (34) control intervals, versus a configured horizon of 10.

limitations: No continuous-time reconstruction or closed-loop counterfactual replay; available checks measure only local plan/endpoint differences at a saved state.
